articles.title: Canal Park Gets $18,500 for Streetlight Upgrade
articles.deck: Residents of Canal Park filled the hall on Friday to ask questions about the plan.
body: Organizers say the project is on schedule and that volunteers are still needed on Friday mornings.
The group has raised $18,500 so far and is asking for help with supplies and food.

articles.title: Volunteers Turn Out for the Spring Cleanup Across Marsh Landing
articles.deck: Residents of Marsh Landing filled the hall on Monday to ask questions about the plan.
body: Organizers say the project is on schedule and that volunteers are still needed on Monday mornings.
The Marsh Landing Improvement Group will post updates on its bulletin board outside the library.
The group has raised $3,400 so far and is asking for help with supplies and food. The plan calls for tool library along Walnut Road, with work expected to start in August.

articles.title: Block Party Returns to Cedar Hollow
articles.deck: Organizers expect about 35 people and say playground upgrade is the main draw.
body: Organizers say the work is on schedule and that volunteers are still needed on Sunday mornings. Nora Schaefer, who has lived on Carver Avenue for 35 years, said the response has been better than anyone expected.
Anyone interested can attend the next planning meeting at St. Brendan’s hall on Sunday at 7 p.m.

articles.title: The Hickory Ridge Recreation Center Opens Book Exchange Box on Cherry Place
articles.deck: The work is expected to take 27 weeks and will be paid for with $48,000 raised locally.
body: The Mill Hill Improvement Group will post updates on its bulletin board outside the library.
The effort began in March when a handful of neighbors met at St. Brendan’s hall to talk about book exchange box.
Anyone interested can attend the next planning meeting at St. Brendan’s hall on Friday at 7 p.m.

articles.title: Plans for Free Tax Clinic Set for Foundry Row This Spring
articles.deck: Doors open at 6 p.m. and the event is free to the public.
body: Children are welcome, and volunteers will be on hand to help with parking and set-up.
The event will be held at the Millrace library, rain or shine, with a backup date set for the following Thursday.

articles.title: Foxglove Heights Elementary Students Earn Regional Honors
articles.deck: Principal Denise Reyes said the school is grateful to families who volunteered this year.
body: Students will meet on Friday afternoons in Millrace Green, and transportation will be provided for those who need it.
Sign-up forms went home in backpacks this week, and the first session is set for January. Principal Denise Reyes said the program was built with help from parents and local volunteers.
The board will review the results at the end of the winter term.

articles.title: Budget Hearing Draws 31 Residents
articles.deck: The vote came after 31 residents spoke at Saturday’s session.
body: Councilmember Renee Mahoney asked for more time to review the proposal, which would cost about $850. Staff recommended approval with two conditions: a traffic study and a public notice period of 30 days.

The ordinance will return to the agenda at the next regular session, unless the chair calls a special meeting first. Residents of Hickory Ridge said they had been asking for action for years, and several brought photographs of the street.
Public works estimates the work will take about 31 weeks once it starts in November.

articles.title: Zoning Board Hears Plan for Summer Concert Series Near Kettle Hill
articles.deck: The vote came after 4 residents spoke at Friday’s session.
body: Councilmember Lydia Orchard asked for more time to review the proposal, which would cost about $3,400.

Staff recommended approval with two conditions: a traffic study and a public notice period of 30 days. Residents of Kettle Hill said they had been asking for action for years, and several brought photographs of the street.
Public works estimates the work will take about 4 weeks once it starts in June.

articles.title: The Foxglove Heights Neighbors Plans After-school Reading Program for Fall
articles.deck: The work is expected to take 21 weeks and will be paid for with $48,000 raised locally.
body: The effort began in December when a handful of neighbors met at the Bellwood Chapel to talk about after-school reading program.

Esther Schaefer, who has lived on Tillman Street for 21 years, said the response has been better than anyone expected. Anyone interested can attend the next planning meeting at the Bellwood Chapel on Sunday at 7 p.m.

articles.title: Hickory Ridge Elementary Teams Head to Summer Tournament
articles.deck: The program begins in June and is open to all students in grade 4 and up.
body: Principal Denise Ingersoll said the program was built with help from parents and local volunteers.
The board will review the results at the end of the summer term. Students will meet on Wednesday afternoons in the Eastgate community hall, and transportation will be provided for those who need it.
Sign-up forms went home in backpacks this week, and the first session is set for June.

articles.title: Theodore Haddad, 82, Bus Driver
articles.deck: Friends remember Theodore Haddad for the many years of service to Marsh Landing.
body: Born in Marsh Landing in the years after the war, Theodore Haddad spent most of a working life in the trades and most of a retirement in the neighborhood.
Services will be held at the parish hall, and donations may be made to the Millrace Library branch in his or her name.

articles.title: Then & Now: Elm Terrace in 1984 and Today
articles.deck: A photo from the Millrace County Historical Society shows the same corner as it looked decades ago.
body: A 1984 photograph from the Millrace County Historical Society shows Elm Terrace from the corner of Hazel Place.
Someone took the same picture from the same spot this month, holding the camera at about the same height.

articles.title: Mill Hill Residents Push for Basketball Court
articles.deck: Organizers expect about 4 people and say basketball court is the main draw.
body: Several residents on Willow Avenue said they had been waiting since 1985 for something like this.
Anyone interested can attend the next planning meeting at the Millrace library on Sunday at 7 p.m.
The group has raised $12,000 so far and is asking for help with supplies and food. The effort began in November when a handful of neighbors met at the Millrace library to talk about basketball court.

articles.title: Marsh Landing Asks Council for Speed Limit Change
articles.deck: Supporters and opponents on Juniper Drive disagreed about cost and timing.
body: Councilmember Edna Szabo asked for more time to review the proposal, which would cost about $12,000. Staff recommended approval with two conditions: a traffic study and a public notice period of 30 days.
Public works estimates the work will take about 29 weeks once it starts in May.
The ordinance will return to the agenda at the next regular session, unless the chair calls a special meeting first.

articles.title: Letter: Thanks to the Foxglove Heights Neighbors
body: To the editor: Please keep the neighborhood watch sign program in the budget. Many of us on Calder Avenue use it every week. I hope the council will listen to the people who turned out at the April meeting.
Thank you for printing this letter, and for all the work the paper does to keep us informed.

To the editor: I have lived on Calder Avenue for 9 years, and I want to say what a difference the Foxglove Heights Neighbors has made. Please keep the neighborhood watch sign program in the budget. Many of us on Calder Avenue use it every week.
Albert Emerson, Foundry Row

articles.title: Cedar Hollow Primary Adds Free Tax Clinic to Summer Schedule
articles.deck: The program begins in November and is open to all students in grade 5 and up.
body: Sign-up forms went home in backpacks this week, and the first session is set for November.

Principal Talia Baptiste said the program was built with help from parents and local volunteers. Students will meet on Wednesday afternoons in the Mill Hill town hall, and transportation will be provided for those who need it.

articles.title: The Upper Commons Historical Society Plans Bus Shelter for Winter
articles.deck: Organizers expect about 16 people and say bus shelter is the main draw.
body: Organizers say the work is on schedule and that volunteers are still needed on Monday mornings. The effort began in April when a handful of neighbors met at the Bellwood Chapel to talk about bus shelter.
Anyone interested can attend the next planning meeting at the Bellwood Chapel on Monday at 7 p.m.

articles.title: Letter: the Hickory Ridge Recreation Center Did a Good Job This Winter
body: To the editor: I hope the council will listen to the people who turned out at the October meeting.
Please keep the second recycling drop-off in the budget. Many of us on Vernon Street use it every week. Thank you for printing this letter, and for all the work the paper does to keep us informed.
To the editor: I have lived on Vernon Street for 24 years, and I want to say what a difference the Hickory Ridge Recreation Center has made.
Wanda Ashby, Tannery Flats
